avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer reduces sorafenib plasma concentrations significantly
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, switch to alternative antidepressant and allow 2-week washout before sorafenib dosing adjustment

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4/2C8 inducer substantially decreases sorafenib bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Use alternative antimicrobial if possible; if required, monitor for reduced sorafenib efficacy and consider dose increase under physician guidance

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate anticoagulant effects and increase bleeding risk with sorafenib
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E to <400 IU daily; monitor for signs of bleeding and adjust if on concurrent anticoagulants

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 induction may modestly reduce sorafenib levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor efficacy; maintain consistent dosing and discuss with prescriber if considering use

caution_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects; combined with sorafenib may increase minor bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor for unusual bruising or bleeding

caution_supplements.name: Curcumin/Turmeric
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition may slightly increase sorafenib exposure
caution_supplements.action: Moderate intake acceptable; inform prescriber of regular use for monitoring

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals
avoid_foods.mechanism: Significantly increases sorafenib absorption (up to 49%), leading to increased toxicity risk and variable bioavailability
avoid_foods.action: Take sorafenib consistently on empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after food); avoid grapefruit and fatty meals

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitor increases sorafenib plasma concentrations and toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Eliminate grapefruit and grapefruit juice from diet entirely during sorafenib therapy

caution_foods.name: Tyramine-rich foods (aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented foods)
caution_foods.mechanism: Theoretical interaction with kinase inhibition pathways; minimal clinical evidence
caution_foods.action: No specific restriction needed, but maintain consistent dietary pattern and report any unusual symptoms

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cabbage, Brussels sprouts)
caution_foods.mechanism: Mild CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 induction at very high intakes
caution_foods.action: Normal consumption is safe; excessive amounts (>3 servings daily) should be discussed with prescriber

monitoring_notes: Sorafenib requires consistent empty-stomach administration for reliable bioavailability; counsel patients to maintain strict adherence to food/supplement restrictions to prevent therapeutic failure or toxicity. Monitor blood pressure, hand-foot skin reactions, and bleeding signs; adjust intake of vitamin K-containing foods minimally and maintain consistency if on concurrent anticoagulation.
